scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, from 590-610/month in Jun-Jul to 1,180-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (F-05).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target) across 2,440 tickets (F-01), so the surge is not a handling-speed issue.
Majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) involve ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED reads (F-03).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (F-02).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600 to over 1,200/month starting August 2026 (F-05), not because dispute handling is slow (within SLA, F-01) or a tariff changed (none occurred, F-04), but because the billing import + validation step is issuing incorrect bills: the majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025, ~59%) are built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimated ones (F-03), showing the defect occurs when accepted reads are processed into bills, not only when reads are missing. A field manual-read completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9,200 accounts, F-02) is a secondary contributor driving estimate-substitution disputes for the remaining accounts.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-12: E-02 still shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9,200 manual-read accounts — the operational shortfall itself stands. It no longer supports that this shortfall is a secondary contributor to the disputed ESTIMATED-read bucket, since E-12 shows that bucket (1,184/1,240) is AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import for high consumption, not manual-read misses.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume doubled because billing is wrong and tickets are handled too slowly/manually; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August caused systematic mis-handling of reads (e.g. wrong read-type acceptance or estimate substitution), producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) from vendor ORG-AMI started failing or degrading around August, causing missing accepted reads and estimate substitution leading to wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read collection/upload from contracted ORG-FIELD (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded around August (e.g. missed routes), causing more estimated bills and disputes.

H-NON-ACCURACY-DISPUTE-DRIVER.statement: Bills may be largely correct; the ticket surge instead reflects a change in dispute reasons/categorization or customer-facing communication rather than an actual rise in billing errors.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) reads, suggesting an error in how actual reads are billed (e.g. tariff application or rate calculation) independent of estimate substitution.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution even when a valid read was received before cutoff and exported; this accounts for 1,184 of 1,240 disputed estimated-read accounts (E-12).

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: Rule BV-17 compares a raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling recorded as 'none', so if the register value is not already in m3 (or in compatible units), legitimate reads could be spuriously flagged as high-consumption and rejected into estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (E-01) shows dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA) across 2440 tickets. This indicates the dispute surge is not explained by slow or inadequate ticket handling, since handling already meets the service target.

Route-log data (E-02) shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, with 9200 manual-read accounts affected. This indicates an actual operational shortfall in manual meter-read collection during the surge period, consistent with more estimated (vs. actual) reads feeding into billing.

E-02 still shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9,200 manual-read accounts — the operational shortfall itself stands. It no longer supports that this shortfall is a secondary contributor to the disputed ESTIMATED-read bucket, since E-12 shows that bucket (1,184/1,240) is AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import for high consumption, not manual-read misses.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 involve ACTUAL reads versus 1240 involving ESTIMATED reads (E-03). This means estimate substitution (the mechanism behind the AMI-export and field-read-failure hypotheses) accounts for only a minority (~41%) of disputed bills; the majority of disputes occur on bills built from actual meter reads, pointing to a cause other than missing/estimated reads for most disputes.

E-03 still shows the disputed-bill counts by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL — that split is unchanged. It no longer means estimate substitution is the field-read-failure or AMI-export-failure mechanism for most of the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputes, since E-12 shows 1,184 of those 1,240 were AMI reads received and exported but rejected at import on a high-consumption rule, not missed/late manual or AMI reads.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff modifications occurred in the logged period. This rules out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism behind erroneous bills on actual-read accounts.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly (will be E-05) shows ticket counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep), confirming that dispute volume roughly doubled starting August 2026 as the scenario describes, and that volume continued rising into September rather than plateauing.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change has occurred this year. As a non-authoritative stakeholder statement it adds no new proof, but it agrees with the already-recorded authoritative E-04 finding (zero tariff-change-log records), reinforcing that a tariff-rate change is not the mechanism behind the disputed bills.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims field reading has been short three readers since July, so routes run late and affected customers receive estimated bills. As a stakeholder statement it is a candidate mechanism explanation for the manual-read shortfall already shown in E-02, not independent proof, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive toward contract headcount increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document confirms the contractual basis for the K-DISPATCH constraint: route priority changes (push_route_update) may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It speaks to governance/authority over the protected dispatch action, not to the root cause of the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log's lagging_routes query (E-09) identifies 14 specific routes with their individual completion rates (e.g. R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity behind the aggregate 0.88-vs-0.95 shortfall already shown in E-02. It supplies the route identifiers needed to correlate the field shortfall with specific estimated-billing accounts (W-WI-ROUTE-PULL) but does not itself speak to why those routes are lagging.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle pull (E-10) returns account/route-level data for 320 accounts estimated in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes. This supplies the billing-side granularity needed to correlate the field route shortfall (E-09's 14 lagging routes) with estimate-substitution billing, but the join itself is not yet computed in this observation.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor AMI Program Engineer) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder report about access/operational status, not a confirmation of AMI read-event content or export health itself; it suggests the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be retriable, but does not itself establish whether the AMI export was failing or missing reads.

mdms-export's authoritative pull for disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (E-12) shows that of 1,240 reads, 1,184 were actually received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 had no read received at all (NO_READ_RECEIVED, not exported). This indicates the billing import validation step — specifically a high-consumption rejection rule — is the dominant mechanism substituting estimates for these disputed accounts, not AMI export failure and, since these are AMI-channel reads, not the manual field-read route shortfall either.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-config's validation rule change log (E-13) shows rule BV-17 — a high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, with unit_scaling="none" — was deployed 2026-08-01, coinciding with the dispute-surge onset; the only other change, BV-09 (2026-03-02), is a cosmetic label-text edit unrelated to billing logic. This confirms DA-RULES did change around August 2026 and ties E-12's REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism to a specific, dated rule deployment.

mdms-export's meter_firmware_units pull (E-14) shows firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record register values in units of "0.1 m3" while legacy firmware v3.x records in whole "m3". Combined with BV-17's raw-register-vs-12-month-m3-history comparison with unit_scaling="none" (E-13), this gives a concrete mechanism by which v4.2 reads would read ~10x higher than actual consumption, consistent with spurious high-consumption rejection (E-12).

Billing-db's own import_status_estimated_disputed query independently corroborates E-12 from the billing side: 1,184 disputed-estimated accounts carry firmware v4.2 and import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while 56 (mixed firmware) have NO_READ_RECEIVED. This confirms the BV-17 high-consumption rejection mechanism tied to v4.2 firmware from a second, independent authoritative source rather than mdms-export alone.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.question: Did the billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) actually change around August 2026, and if so what changed?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the billing-import-defect mechanism underlying the root problem and determines what the billing-config review must target.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution_path: Pull the billing-config rule change log for Jul-Sep 2026 and diff against the prior rule set.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-config review as read-only diagnostic only; no bill adjustment is proposed until the specific rule defect is confirmed.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution: Resolved by E-13: billing import validation rules did change around August 2026 — rule BV-17, a high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none', was deployed 2026-08-01; the only other change (BV-09, 2026-03-02) was a cosmetic label edit.

U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.question: Is the vendor AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded in a way that affects accepted-read quality, given mdms-export is DEGRADED and access to disputed-estimated read events is ACCESS_PENDING?
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.decision_impact: If AMI export quality were implicated it would reopen H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE as a contributing mechanism; currently out of active scope since mdms-export has no working fallback.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution_path: Wait for ORG-AMI to provision mdms-export access, then pull read_events_for_disputed_estimated; until then rely on the billing-db read-type data already captured in E-03.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI export health as unverified and out of current diagnostic scope; root-cause work proceeds on the ACTUAL-read billing-import defect and field manual-read shortfall only.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution: E-12 shows the AMI export is largely functioning for disputed-estimated accounts: 1,184 of 1,240 reads were received before cutoff and exported to billing; only 56 had no read received, so export/delivery degradation is not the primary driver of estimate substitution for this population.

U-DISPUTE-REASON-BREAKDOWN.question: What specific billing error pattern (e.g., rate misapplication, duplicate charges, unit errors) characterizes the 1,785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills?
U-DISPUTE-REASON-BREAKDOWN.decision_impact: Determines the exact defect to document for root-cause confirmation and whether one or multiple distinct error patterns exist.
U-DISPUTE-REASON-BREAKDOWN.resolution_path: Pull itemized charge breakdown for the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills from billing-db and classify by error pattern.
U-DISPUTE-REASON-BREAKDOWN.safe_placeholder: Continue read-only itemized analysis of disputed ACTUAL-read bills; no bill writes until the pattern is classified.

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.question: Is the route completion shortfall (E-02) actually caused by a staffing gap since July as SH-FIELD claims (E-07, non-authoritative, headcount-increase incentive), or by another operational cause?
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.decision_impact: Does not change the current estimate-rejection remediation scope, but determines whether a separate staffing-related remedy is warranted for the field route-completion shortfall.
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.resolution_path: Independently verify via field-dispatch scheduling logs or HR headcount data rather than relying solely on SH-FIELD's self-report (E-07).
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion shortfall as a separate, unrelated known issue outside this problem's scope; do not act on SH-FIELD's staffing claim without independent verification.

U-METRIC-VALIDITY-DISPUTE-BASE.question: Is Jun 2026 (610) or Jul 2026 (590) the correct pre-August baseline for measuring a return to normal dispute volume, given month-to-month variance?
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-DISPUTE-BASE.decision_impact: Affects what baseline value SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-TARGET is measured against; picking the wrong baseline could prematurely declare success or failure.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-DISPUTE-BASE.resolution_path: Collect additional months of pre-August baseline dispute volume to determine a stable baseline before fixing the target threshold.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-DISPUTE-BASE.safe_placeholder: Use the lower of the two observed baseline months (590, Jul 2026) as the conservative target threshold until more baseline data is available.

U-AFFECTED-POPULATION-SCOPE.question: How many total accounts beyond the 1,240 disputed sample have v4.2-firmware AMI reads rejected under BV-17 for high consumption, i.e. what is the full population needing bill correction?
U-AFFECTED-POPULATION-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether flagging and future bill-correction work must cover more than the 1,240 disputed accounts; underestimating scope would leave unflagged accounts billed incorrectly.
U-AFFECTED-POPULATION-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query mdms-export for all v4.2-firmware accounts with billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not only the 1,240-account disputed sample, to size the full remediation population.
U-AFFECTED-POPULATION-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Limit diagnostic correlation and flagging to the 1,184 confirmed-affected disputed accounts (E-12); treat any broader population as unconfirmed until queried.
U-AFFECTED-POPULATION-SCOPE.resolution: Billing-db's own v4.2/REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION account list (E-16) totals exactly 1,184 accounts, identical to the already-known disputed-sample count (E-12/E-15), suggesting no larger affected population in DA-BILL; full confirmation still requires joining with mdms-export reads_for_accounts (now access-provisioned per CL-04/E-11) to verify from the AMI side.

U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the nightly AMI register-read handoff H-MDMS-BILL (ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) delivering complete and semantically valid reads, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN?
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If the handoff is dropping or corrupting reads beyond the already-exported 1,184 rejected records, correlation and flagging could miss additional affected accounts or misattribute cause.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Request handoff validation (completeness/schema conformance) comparing mdms-export records against billing-db import records for the affected period.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Rely only on the already-exported-and-rejected 1,184 account records (E-12), which are confirmed delivered; do not assume additional undelivered reads behave the same until the handoff is validated.

A-IMPORT-VALIDATION-DEFECT.statement: The billing import + validation step (rather than a confirmed specific rule change) is assumed to be where actual-read bills are mis-processed, since no billing-config (DA-RULES) evidence has yet been pulled.

A-AGGREGATE-FIRMWARE-UNIFORMIT.statement: The single firmware='v4.2' value attached to the 1,184-count REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION aggregate record (E-12) is assumed to mean essentially all of those reads came from v4.2 meters, since the record is a count aggregate rather than per-account firmware detail.

A-RULES-LOG-COMPLETE.statement: The billing-config validation_rule_changes log (E-13) is assumed to have captured all relevant rule changes near August 2026, even though DA-RULES's overall completeness is still marked UNKNOWN.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, from 590-610/month in Jun-Jul to 1,180-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target) across 2,440 tickets (E-01), ruling out handling speed as the cause.

v4.2-firmware AMI meters (rolled out 2026-06) record register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3, unlike legacy v3.x meters (E-14).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-05), not from slow handling (within SLA, E-01) or a tariff change (none occurred, E-04). top_hypotheses: H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: A change to the billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August caused systematic mis-handling of reads (e.g. wrong read-type acceptance or estimate substitution), producing incorrect bills. [SUPPORTED]

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution even when a valid read was received before cutoff and exported; this accounts for 1,184 of 1,240 disputed estimated-read accounts (E-12). [CONFIRMED]

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT: Rule BV-17 compares a raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling recorded as 'none', so if the register value is not already in m3 (or in compatible units), legitimate reads could be spuriously flagged as high-consumption and rejected into estimate substitution. framing_assertion.rationale: Initial request from SH-CS asserts the August-September ticket doubling is caused by incorrect bills that an AI agent can auto-answer and auto-fix, per scenario initial_request text.

hypotheses.statement: Dispute volume doubled because billing is wrong and tickets are handled too slowly/manually; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills would resolve it.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-CS's framing (role: Customer Service Director, noted bias: 'frames the issue as a response-speed problem'); it also conflicts with K-BILLWRITE which forbids automated bill writes, so if adopted uncritically the proposed solution is partly infeasible.

hypotheses.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August caused systematic mis-handling of reads (e.g. wrong read-type acceptance or estimate substitution), producing incorrect bills.
hypotheses.rationale: ORG-UTIL owns DA-RULES (billing import validation rule change log) and the meter-to-cash process explicitly lists 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' as a step; a rule change there is a plausible single-point root cause distinct from any staffing or response-speed story.

hypotheses.statement: AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) from vendor ORG-AMI started failing or degrading around August, causing missing accepted reads and estimate substitution leading to wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and DA-MDMS completeness are both UNKNOWN and require vendor-provisioned access (mdms-export), so an undetected vendor-side delivery problem is a live alternative to the requester's framing.

hypotheses.statement: Manual meter read collection/upload from contracted ORG-FIELD (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded around August (e.g. missed routes), causing more estimated bills and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: H-FIELD-BILL delivery_status/semantic_validity are UNKNOWN and SH-FIELD has a noted potential_bias to attribute problems to staffing, so route completion data (DA-ROUTE) is needed to test this independently of that stated bias.

hypotheses.rationale: G-1 frames the goal only as 'dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills', leaving open whether disputes track real billing errors or something else recorded only in DA-TICKET; this would redirect the fix toward CRM/communication rather than the meter-to-cash pipeline.

proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-05), not from slow handling (within SLA, E-01) or a tariff change (none occurred, E-04). For 1,184 of 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts, AMI reads were received and exported but rejected at billing import under rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13), which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none'; because v4.2-firmware meters (rollout 2026-06) record in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-14), their reads appear roughly 10x too high and are spuriously flagged high-consumption, forcing estimate substitution (E-12). symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, from 590-610/month in Jun-Jul to 1,180-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target) across 2,440 tickets (E-01), ruling out handling speed as the cause.

Of 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts, 1,184 had AMI reads received and exported but rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, a high-consumption check with unit_scaling=none, was deployed 2026-08-01, coincident with the dispute-surge onset (E-13).
v4.2-firmware AMI meters (rolled out 2026-06) record register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3, unlike legacy v3.x meters (E-14).
The majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025, ~59%) carry ACTUAL reads (E-03), a bucket not explained by the BV-17 mechanism.
causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 AMI meters (rolled out 2026-06) record register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than whole m3 (E-14).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling='none' (E-13).
For v4.2-metered accounts this raw-vs-m3 mismatch makes legitimate reads appear ~10x higher than true consumption, triggering BV-17's high-consumption check.
1,184 of the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts had AMI reads received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12).
Rejected reads are replaced with an estimated bill instead of the actual read, producing a bill the customer perceives as wrong.
Customers file dispute tickets over these estimate-substituted bills; this is not explained by slow handling (E-01) or a tariff change (E-04).
Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, from 590-610/month in Jun-Jul to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026, coincident with BV-17's deployment date (E-05, E-13).

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) originally asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and "fix whatever is causing the wrong bills" (CL-01), after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-05). Investigation ruled out slow ticket handling (E-01: within SLA) and a tariff change (E-04/E-06: none occurred). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1) attributing part of the surge to a field manual-read staffing shortfall (E-02, E-07) was invalidated once E-12 showed that bucket of disputes was actually AMI reads rejected at billing import, not missed field reads. The confirmed successor problem (PD-1@v2) is that billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history without unit scaling, and v4.2-firmware meters (rolled out 2026-06, E-14) report in 0.1 m3 units, so their reads appear ~10x too high and are spuriously rejected as high-consumption (E-12/E-15), forcing estimate substitution for 1,184 of 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts. This mechanism was independently confirmed from both mdms-export and billing-db (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17), sizing the full affected population at exactly 1,184 accounts. The majority dispute bucket (1,785 of 3,025 ACTUAL-read disputes, E-03) remains unexplained. The release delivers only a read-only review and flagging of the confirmed BV-17/firmware mechanism and the 1,184 affected accounts for manual Billing Operations follow-up; it does not fix the rule, correct any bills, or build the originally requested ticket-answering agent. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items on hold.
